content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity as the reason to leave the point UNDERDETERMINED, which is the kind of ground K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED': one reading forbids only treating a lone verse's silence as decisive for underdetermination, while the other forbids any underdetermination resting on absence of explicit textual resolution; the judge's words fit the forbidden latter reading.","why":"The judge's stated basis is the absence of explicit textual resolution of paternity, so it makes underdetermination rest on the kind of non-explicit single-verse silence K-S2 forbids."}
